overall: Atlanta is heating up aggressively this morning, with the running max already at 93.2°F by 11:50 ET and still climbing at +3.6°F/hr. Conditions are hotter than the NBM suggested (NBM currently pins TMAX at 93.2°F, matching the current reading rather than the eventual peak), and with peak timing still roughly 2.5 hours away near 14:30 ET, significant additional warming is expected. A slight chance of afternoon storms (20% PoP) exists but is unlikely to meaningfully suppress the high given the current trajectory and mostly-sunny sky cover.
forecast_obs_notes: There is notable model disagreement: GFS is bullish at 99.4°F, ECMWF sits at 96.7°F, HRRR at 95.2°F, and NBM at 93.2°F — a 6.2°F spread. The NBM is clearly already behind observed conditions, lending more credibility to the warmer GFS/ECMWF solutions. NWS text forecasts a high near 96°F, which aligns roughly with the HRRR/ECMWF cluster and may prove conservative given the current warming rate.
max_temp_prediction: With 93.2°F already in the books at midday and ~2.5 hours of heating remaining before the ~14:30 ET expected peak, simple extrapolation (even with decelerating velocity) points to a final high in the 97–99°F range. The META model — the most reliable fusion signal — places the 98-99°F even bucket as the clear leader at 37.0%, followed by 100-101°F and 96-97°F each at ~19.7%. The active Kalshi even-bucket top of 98-99°F at 27.3% aligns well with META and the current trajectory; confidence is moderate-to-good given strong intraday signal but meaningful model spread.
